title: Protesters rally against autonomus vehicles in DC
key_facts: Dozens of Uber drivers, union workers and faith leaders rallied outside the John Wilson Building on Tuesday against a bill to bring Waymo and other robotaxi services to Washington, D.C.
The Autonomous Vehicle Deployment Authorization Amendment Act of 2026 would cap each operator at 200 vehicles until 1 Jan 2028.
It also sets rules for level three, four and five autonomous systems.
Sponsor Charles Allen says it presents an opportunity to improve traffic and consumer choice.
Driver Helen Raynor says she earns up to $1,000 extra a month from ride-hail and fears losing it.
quote_evidence: Dozens of Uber drivers, union workers and faith leaders gathered Tuesday outside the John Wilson Building to rally against a proposal that would bring Waymo and other autonomous driving services to the city.
The bill is sponsored by Ward 6 Council member Charles Allen, who said introducing autonomous vehicles “presents an opportunity to improve traffic and consumer choice in the District.”
why_it_matters_hint: Ride-hail drivers push back as a U.S. capital weighs allowing robotaxis.
notes: NBC4 page was video only (headline and short description); WTOP read instead. FOX 5 DC and WJLA carry the same rally.
